already-have.reason: Not implemented and not squarely tracked. All four repo_evidence facts are true today. Only the USB arm wipes on PinLocked (secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:123,150,159-164; fn at :190, private to that file). The boot-interactive arm (secure/src/main.rs:4198-4206) and the PendSV arm (main.rs:4587-4597) show "PIN locked / power cycle", log "no wipe performed on this path" and break. The boot wipe check (main.rs:1933-1936) keys only on is_wipe_armed() or page124 >= MAX_ATTEMPTS. reconcile_pin_attempts (nsc/mod.rs:1663-1716) adds a wipe only for E120_used > page124, and SE050 is not a boot input. So an SE-originated PinLocked (SE050 AuthMethodBlocked via se050/mod.rs:2868, or OPTIGA E120 curr>=limit via optiga/mod.rs:2432) with page 124 < 10 leaves both halves intact when entered on the LCD arms, and the next boot does not wipe. The proposal overstates the consequence: after the boot arm breaks, the device continues to USB init, so any companion CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK reaches the wiping arm, and the ordinary 10-wrong-PIN case is already covered by a deferred wipe at next boot (page 124 is pre-charged to 10). The real defect is trigger-dependent behaviour plus claim-vs-code drift, not a counter bypass. The proposal also collides with the open fix direction of #104/#120 (do not wipe on an uncorroborated SE lockout status) and with the open post-wipe brick #168, so it cannot land standalone at P1.
already-have.corrections:
1. Threat wording: "attempt-counter bypass" is wrong. gated_unlock pre-charges page 124 on every arm (nsc/mod.rs:1396 onward), so no arm gives extra guesses. The defect is an inconsistent lockout response: the wipe is deferred to next boot on the page-124 path and absent on the SE-originated path with page 124 < MAX.
2. "Locked-but-unwiped" is not terminal. After the boot arm breaks, boot proceeds to USB init (main.rs:4222 onward), and a companion CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK then hits cmd_request_unlock.rs:159-164 and wipes. The gap is for a device used without a companion, or one that is power-cycled.
3. The boot arm has no MAX check on PinIncorrect (main.rs:4208-4211), unlike the USB arm (cmd_request_unlock.rs:126-151). The 10th wrong PIN shows "Wrong PIN / try again" with no "LAST ATTEMPT" warning, the 11th entry shows "PIN locked / power cycle", and the wipe happens at the next boot via main.rs:1935. This is the actual Trezor-parity delta (storage.c:1224-1230 wipes inline).
4. Claim-vs-code drift to record: CLAUDE.md invariant #2 ("AuthMethodBlocked still maps to PinLocked and the wipe path"), se050/mod.rs:2860-2862 and the gated_unlock doc (nsc/mod.rs:1362-1363, "Caller is responsible for running trigger_lockout_wipe") hold for one of three callers.
5. The proposed boot check "SE says locked while page 124 < MAX → wipe_armed" cannot be evaluated at boot for SE050: the attribute read is denied with 0x6986 and a VERIFY probe would itself consume an attempt (nsc/mod.rs:1649-1655, #200). It can only be done by arming the page-125 flag (hw/flash.rs:682 arm_wipe_flag) at the moment the verdict is seen.
6. Arming or wiping on an SE-originated PinLocked must follow the #104/#120 direction (corroborate across reinit plus a fresh session, with a page-124 floor), not precede it. Otherwise the forged-bare-0x6986 one-frame wipe, today reachable only over USB, extends to the two LCD arms. The proposal's "R-MAC-authenticated status" gate is not available for the bare-SW case as the code stands (#104 cites scp03.rs:605-627).
7. Dependency: #168 (post-lockout wipe is an unrecoverable brick on real hardware) is open. Making wipes more eager before it is fixed increases brick exposure; this is what the proposal calls pin-01.
8. Also in scope: pin_attempt_log labels every PinLocked as AlreadyAtMax (nsc/mod.rs:1628), so an SE-originated lockout is indistinguishable in the #715 diagnostic log. The e2e wipe test hand-mirrors trigger_lockout_wipe (main.rs:3562) and should call the shared function once it moves.
9. Keep the #715 text pins: "PIN locked / power cycle" is pinned in secure/src/ui/px/status_map.rs:610,776; the AlreadyAtMax branch must keep that text.
10. Cost S is optimistic: three arms, a px status map, the ordering against #104/#120/#168, and no silicon test is possible without burning an SE050 UserID (#715 comment). M is more honest.
11. I did not re-run any build or test; this is a source read. The advisor call was rate-limited, so there was no second review.

already-have.untracked_delta:
No issue tracks any of the following.
(a) The boot-interactive and PendSV arms never call the wipe on PinLocked; only the USB arm does.
(b) An SE-originated PinLocked with page 124 < MAX on those arms leaves no durable marker (page-125 flag not armed), so the next boot neither wipes nor knows.
(c) The boot arm lacks the remaining==0 / LAST ATTEMPT handling the USB arm has; the 10th wrong PIN yields a deferred, next-boot wipe.
(d) trigger_lockout_wipe is a private fn in cmd_request_unlock.rs with a hand-copied mirror in the e2e test (main.rs:3562), instead of one shared function in nsc/mod.rs.
(e) Doc and comment drift claiming AuthMethodBlocked → wipe unconditionally (CLAUDE.md invariant #2, se050/mod.rs:2860, nsc/mod.rs:1362).
(f) pin_attempt_log collapses SE-originated PinLocked into AlreadyAtMax (nsc/mod.rs:1628).
decision_conflicts: No recorded owner decision is contradicted. The #715 fix (commit 255a9554; main.rs:4199-4205 and 4588-4596) deliberately made these arms say 'no wipe performed'; the proposal keeps that for AlreadyAtMax, so it is compatible, but the px status-map pins (secure/src/ui/px/status_map.rs:610,776) must keep passing.

Tension with open triage #104 and #120: their recommended fix is to corroborate AuthMethodBlocked/PinLocked across reinit plus a fresh session and a page-124 floor before wiping. The proposal's 'treat SE-says-locked with page 124 < MAX as wipe_armed' runs the other way unless sequenced after them. The proposal's own risks field concedes this.
Tension with #168 (F23, post-wipe brick; docs/security/adversarial-review/findings/full-project-sweep-2026-07-18-discovery.md:360): more wipe triggers before that fix means more bricks.

CLAUDE.md invariant #2 and #200: SE050 attempt state is unreadable at boot (0x6986), so the boot-check half of the proposal is only implementable through a flag armed at verdict time. Reading SE050 at boot would need the separately reviewed policy/silicon decision that CLAUDE.md says is required.

live_defect.reachable_in_production_config: Yes in principle: the boot and PendSV arms are compiled for stm32u585 dual-SE builds, and nothing in the arms is feature-gated to dev. Not demonstrated on silicon; an SE-originated lockout with page 124 < 10 needs a counter desync (page-124 rollback, a forged or faulted status, or E120 lifetime exhaustion).
live_defect.evidence: secure/src/main.rs:4198-4206 and 4587-4597 break without wiping or arming page 125, while secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:159-164 wipes on the same verdict. secure/src/main.rs:1935-1936 does not see an SE-originated lockout at the next boot. Mitigated because a later USB CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK wipes, and the ordinary 10-wrong-PIN case wipes at next boot.

feasible.reason: The core asymmetry is real and in the shipping path: only the USB arm wipes on PinLocked; the boot-interactive and PendSV arms print "PIN locked / power cycle" and break. Routing all three through one shared wipe helper does close it and is buildable in firmware only on pq1 (no board change). But the threat statement is overstated in three ways. (1) It is not an attempt-counter bypass: no arm grants an extra PIN guess, because gated_unlock precharges page 124 on every arm and short-circuits at MAX. (2) "E120 exhaustion ... the next boot does not wipe either" is false: reconcile_pin_attempts wipes at next boot whenever E120 > page 124. (3) SE050-originated PinLocked only surfaces when OPTIGA ACCEPTED the PIN (dual_se.rs discards the SE050 result on OPTIGA PinIncorrect), so a wrong-PIN attacker can never produce it; that case is a correct-PIN user with a blocked or forged-blocked SE050, and it self-converges to a wipe after at most 10 boots because each attempt leaves page 124 charged. The real residual is narrower: after the 10th wrong PIN at the boot or idle prompt (the primary prompt on a display device) both SE halves stay intact until the next powered boot or the next USB unlock, a chip-off window the USB arm does not leave, plus a display/behaviour inconsistency. That is defence-in-depth parity, P2 not P1.
feasible.corrections:
1. Threat rewording: drop "attempt-counter bypass". Correct statement: "deferred wipe on two of three unlock arms; halves remain intact on both SEs after lockout until the next boot or USB unlock". 
2. E120 claim is wrong: E120 exhaustion with page 124 < MAX gives e120 > mcu, and boot reconcile (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1693-1716, called at main.rs:1794-1801 in dual-se non-prodtest builds) wipes. Only the SE050 leg is invisible at boot. 
3. SE050-originated PinLocked requires OPTIGA Ok (secure/src/dual_se.rs:370-404), i.e. the correct PIN was entered. Making the boot/PendSV arms wipe immediately therefore wipes a user who typed the right PIN whenever a bare 0x6986 appears. Bare error status words carry no R-MAC (secure/src/se050/scp03.rs:551-558), so the proposal's own mitigation "gate on an R-MAC-authenticated status" is not realisable for an error SW: there is never an authenticated 0x6986. The only workable form is: on SE-originated PinLocked, arm the page-125 flag and re-confirm on the next boot with a fresh SCP03 session before wiping. This already applies to the USB arm today (#104/#105). 
4. The clause "add 'SE says locked while page 124 < MAX' to the boot attempts_exhausted check" is not an S-cost item: SE050 attempt attributes are policy-denied (0x6986) at boot and a VERIFY probe consumes an attempt; CLAUDE.md invariant #2 says a three-way boot input needs a separately reviewed SE050 policy/backend and silicon decision. A create_session-only probe (lockout surfaces at create_session per se050/apdu.rs:745-754) might work without a PIN but is unverified on silicon (session-pending Finding A3). Replace this clause with "arm the page-125 wipe flag (hw::flash::arm_wipe_flag, flash.rs:682) on the PinLocked arm", which the existing boot check at main.rs:1935-1954 already honours. 
5. Missing from the proposal: the boot and PendSV PinIncorrect arms do not check the post-bump count at all (main.rs:4209-4212, 4597-4603). The USB arm wipes on the 10th wrong PIN via the fail-in remaining_after check (cmd_request_unlock.rs:112-150); the other two say "Wrong PIN, try again" and only report lock on an 11th entry. Trezor parity ("ctr+1 >= PIN_MAX_TRIES") needs that check ported, not just the PinLocked arm. 
6. CounterUnstable (two page-124 reads disagree, nsc/mod.rs:1430-1437) and the duress-wipe path (nsc/mod.rs:1541-1547) also return PinLocked. The shared helper must not double-wipe after a duress wipe or print a false screen; and a wipe on a single flash read mismatch at the boot prompt is an FI-triggerable destructive action, same as on USB today. 
7. trigger_lockout_wipe is not "FI-shaped" itself (cmd_request_unlock.rs:190-211 is a plain function); the fail-in shape lives in its caller. Moving it must carry the fail-in caller pattern to each arm. 
8. Trezor precedent is accurate: storage/storage.c:1223-1230 wipes at ctr+1 >= PIN_MAX_TRIES inside the single unlock(). Minor: line range is 1223-1230, not 1224-1240. 
9. Cost S holds only for the reduced scope (shared helper + count check + flag arm). With a silicon-validated SE050 boot probe it is M and mixed with a silicon decision. Running factory_reset_admin from PendSV is plausible (gated_unlock already does SE I/O and flash writes there) but its duration against IWDG in that context is untested. 
10. Any change needs the pq1 bench caveat: no LCD on the bench board, so the WIPING / WALLET WIPED screens cannot be evidence; verify via SE state and page 124/125.

live_defect.evidence: secure/src/main.rs:4198-4207 (boot-interactive PinLocked arm: show_status + break, no wipe) and main.rs:4587-4598 (PendSV twin); main.rs:4209-4212 and 4597-4603 (PinIncorrect arms never check the post-bump count); secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:112-164 is the only place that calls trigger_lockout_wipe (lines 123, 150, 163), defined privately at :190. Boot wipe trigger is page-125 flag or page 124 >= MAX only (main.rs:1935-1954). After break the boot arm falls through to USB init and 'Gateway ready' (main.rs:4222-4258) with the device locked and unwiped. NOT as described: E120 exhaustion is caught by reconcile (nsc/mod.rs:1693-1716); SE050 AuthMethodBlocked reaches the caller only when OPTIGA returned Ok (dual_se.rs:372-403).
live_defect.reachable_in_production_config: Yes. The boot-interactive arm is gated only by cfg(not(feature = "e2e-test")) (main.rs:3969) and the PendSV handler by cfg(all(not(test), feature = "stm32u585")) (main.rs:4494); both are in PROD_SHIP_FEATURES (Makefile:2718: stm32u585, dual-se, ui-lcd, usb, mode-production, optiga-hw-counter). duress-pin is not in that set, so the duress-wipe false-screen variant is bench-only. Caveat: no mode-production + optiga image links today (S-2 fence), so 'shipping' means the intended ship feature set.
live_defect.severity: Low to medium. No extra PIN guesses and no key exposure by itself. Effects: (a) after 10 wrong PINs at the boot or idle prompt, both XOR halves stay on the SEs until the next powered boot or USB unlock, a chip-off window that the USB arm closes immediately; (b) behaviour differs by entry arm, and the 10th wrong PIN shows 'Wrong PIN, try again' instead of locking; (c) a correct-PIN user with a blocked or forged-blocked SE050 sees 'PIN locked / power cycle' on up to 10 boots before page 124 reaches MAX and the boot check wipes.
